Secondary Hacks — More Ways to Find Startups

LinkedIn is your core search stack. These five secondary hacks help you surface vertical-AI startups — sector-specific AI at the application layer — that most people never find. Same playbook, more places to look.

Google Reddit Product Hunt Wellfound X / Twitter
Hack 1 of 5

Simple Google Search (Your Fastest Quick Win)

Before anything else, try a direct Google search. Many early-stage vertical-AI startups show up on websites, demo lists, or tech articles before they appear anywhere else.

1Try searches like:
"vertical AI fintech startup 2025" "AI SDR startup" "AI recruiting software startup"
Swap in your sector — fintech, HR, CRM, sales — and the freshest names surface fast.
A plain Google query, scoped to your sector and year.
Hack 2 of 5

Reddit Communities

Reddit is one of the best places to spot very early startups — founders share prototypes, ask for feedback, and post progress long before they appear anywhere else.

r/startups r/entrepreneur r/artificial

Or any subreddit tied to your chosen sector (fintech, recruiting, sales). Use Reddit's search bar to jump straight into relevant threads.

It's raw, real, and full of early signals — likely to become a favorite search spot.
Browse sector subreddits for the earliest founder signals.
Hack 3 of 5

Product Hunt (New Launches Every Day)

Founded by Ryan Hoover in 2013, Product Hunt began as a simple way to share cool new products with friends. It grew into a global community where creators and tech enthusiasts discover the latest apps, tools, and startups.

Startups launch their products here, and users vote, share feedback, and follow each company's progress.
Product Hunt's daily launch feed.
Hack 3 of 5 · How to use it

How Product Hunt Helps You Find Startups

Use the search bar to find startups in specific categories. Each listing shows upvotes, reviews, and a detailed product description — so you can judge which vertical-AI startups look most promising.

  • Search a category — e.g. AI CRM or AI sales
  • Read upvotes to gauge traction
  • Scan reviews and the founder's comments
Upvotes + reviews = a fast read on which application-layer startups have early pull.
Search a category, then sort by traction.
Hack 4 of 5

Wellfound (formerly AngelList Talent)

Thousands of early-stage startups list themselves on Wellfound. Use it to quickly find new startups that match the investment thesis.

1Open Discover in the top menu
2Search keywords for vertical AI:
"vertical AI fintech" "AI CRM" "AI recruiting" "AI SDR / sales"
wellfound.com/discover
Discover Startups
vertical AI fintechAI CRMAI recruiting
Use Discover + sector keywords to list matching startups.
Hack 4 of 5 · Then verify

From Search Result to Thesis Fit

In the example, a search for "AI CRM" returned two startups. The next step is to use AI to pull more detail on each and confirm they fit the thesis — application-layer, vertical AI, seed / Series A.

  • Run the search for your sector
  • Use AI to research each result
  • Keep only the ones aligned to the thesis
Search returns candidates — you confirm vertical-AI thesis fit before adding them.
Search "AI CRM," then verify each result against the thesis.
Hack 5 of 5

X (Twitter)

X is a hub where startup founders and investors have real-time, public conversations. Explore with relevant hashtags to catch emerging vertical-AI startups and build-in-public projects.

1Start with these hashtags:
#startups #VC #founders #AIagents
Layer in sector tags like #fintech or #SaaS to zero in on your vertical.
Search hashtags to surface live founder chatter.
